items.title: ChatGPT will now make you animated GIFs
items.excerpt: OpenAI is making ChatGPT image generation faster, too.
items.rationale: New release: ChatGPT image generation (Images 2.6) now outputs animated GIFs and runs faster, so designers can make motion assets for social and UI mockups straight from the chat.

items.title: Accelerating engineering for the physical world
items.excerpt: OpenAI says GPT-6 Astra designed a Codex hardware device with no direct human edits: it set the functional requirements and handled the look, the enclosure, the PCB and the software integration. The post also covers models that prepare drawings and set up simulations.
items.rationale: Primary source: OpenAI says a model carried a hardware product from requirements through industrial design, enclosure and PCB with no direct human edits. That is a clear marker for where AI-assisted product design is going.

items.title: Tripo AI launches Agentic Canvas for node-based 3D workflows
items.excerpt: Explore Tripo AI's Agentic Canvas, an innovative tool for creating 3D workflows on a visual node-based platform.
items.rationale: New product: Tripo's node-based agentic canvas chains AI 3D generation steps into repeatable pipelines. 3D and product designers can try it right away.

items.title: nCircle Tech launches nVibe AI app builder
items.excerpt: nCircle Tech launches nVibe AI app builder. AEC professionals describe the workflow and AI application platform builds the app
items.rationale: New release: AEC professionals describe a workflow in plain language and nVibe builds the app, bringing vibe-coding to architecture and engineering teams.

items.title: I ran the same Claude design request 4 times. Only the reference hand-off changed.
items.excerpt: Ask Claude for a design and you often get something that looks like a template you've seen before....
items.rationale: Controlled experiment: the same Claude design prompt run four ways, changing only how the references were handed over. It shows designers how to avoid template-looking output in their next prompt.
